claims.explanation: SC-9 is a naphthalenesulfonamide PKC activator that kills cells with high PKC-pathway dependence, particularly those with TP53 loss and RAS/RTK-MAPK activation that create a pro-proliferative signaling context requiring PKC. The strongest pattern is enrichment of TP53 mutations and RAS/BRAF pathway mutations in sensitive lines, while protective lines often retain wild-type TP53 or have mutations in chromatin remodelers (ARID1A, SMARCA4) that may buffer PKC-driven stress responses.

features.basis: TP53 mutation is highly enriched in sensitive lines (18/20) vs resistant lines (13/20), suggesting loss of p53-mediated survival/apoptosis control sensitizes to PKC activation
KRAS mutations appear in multiple sensitive lines (OV7, RKN, PATU8988T, NCIH1792) and may create MAPK-driven dependency that PKC activation exacerbates
BRAF mutations in sensitive melanoma lines (UACC62, G361) and MDAMB361 suggest MAPK pathway activation sensitizes to PKC activation
NRAS mutations in sensitive lines (RD, NCIH1299) and resistant lines (IPC298, SKNSH) show mixed pattern but may contribute with other lesions
ARID1A mutations are enriched in resistant lines (COLO792, KU1919, HS766T) and may buffer PKC-driven stress through chromatin remodeling
SMARCA4 mutations appear in resistant lines (COV434, NCIH1573, NCIH841, SKNSH) suggesting SWI/SNF loss protects from PKC activation
CDKN2A mutations in sensitive lines (MHHES1, RD, MDAMB361, HARA) may enhance proliferation and PKC dependence
NF1 mutations in sensitive lines (RD, MDAMB361, YD8) may activate RAS-MAPK and increase PKC sensitivity
PIK3CA mutations in sensitive lines (MDAMB361, MKN1) suggest PI3K pathway activation may cooperate with PKC activation
PTEN mutations in sensitive melanoma lines (UACC62) and resistant glioma (U118MG) show mixed pattern but may contribute to PI3K-driven sensitivity
ATM mutations in sensitive lines (RKN, TE9) may impair DNA damage response and enhance sensitivity to PKC-mediated stress
KMT2D mutations in sensitive lines (TE9, LUDLU1) suggest epigenetic dysregulation may increase PKC dependence
